To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel image-guided prostate intervention approach that uses image synthesis to learn a joint appearance model of MRI and TRUS images.
we present an approach for MRI-TRUS fusion using image synthesis that is based on a joint model of MRI and TRUS appearance, and we show preliminary results of this method.
we have developed a method for synthesizing TRUS images from MR images, and that the synthesized TRUS images can be registered with the TRUS image using standard intensity-based registration methods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a robust, accurate and fast image registration method that can be used to fuse pre-procedure MRI and intra-procedure TRUS for image-guided biopsy procedures.
the following questions: (i) can the appearance of TRUS images be accurately synthesized using a joint model of MRI and TRUS image appearance?
the development of a robust and accurate MRI-TRUS fusion method for use in image-guided prostate biopsy procedures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to synthesize a patient’s corresponding TRUST image appearance from the MRI.
the proposed method is able to synthesize TRUS-like appearance from MRI and the synthesized TRUS images can be successfully registered to real TRUS images.
the preliminary results of our approach are encouraging, and we plan to further develop and test our approach in future work.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

this approach can potentially improve MRI-TRUS fusion accuracy by incorporating internal prostate structures into a joint model for image synthesis, and thus, potentially improving the accuracy and robustness of MRI-TRUS intensity-based registration.
we are able to use the joint model learned from the large database to generate TRUS images that are similar in appearance to the actual TRUS images.
we have developed an image synthesis framework to cast a difficult, non-linear multi-modal registration problem to a mono-modal registration problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we show that image synthesis can potentially be a powerful tool to help address the challenging problem of MRI-TRUS fusion.
the synthesis of TRUS images from MRIs is possible and can provide a promising approach to MRI-TRUS fusion.
we show that it is possible to use a large database of MRI and TRUS pairs to learn an appearance model that can be used to generate synthetic TRUS images.
